source_text:
Ἥντινα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου θείαν βίβλον συνηθῶς εἰς χεῖρας ἀναλαβών, τὰς περὶ τούτου κειμένας
προαγγελτικὰς μαρτυρίας ἐγγράφως εὑρήσεις· ὧν μαλιστά σε, δέσποτα, πυκνοτέρᾳ τῇ μελέτῃ προσέχειν παρακαλῶ, διὰ τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν κατὰ τὴν αὐτόθι γεγραμμένων ἀκολουθίαν, τῶν ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν προαναφωνηθέντων, πολλῆς μετ' εὐλαβείας δεομένων τῆς παρατηρήσεως, πρὸς τὸ μηδεμίαν ἐξ ἀντικειμένης ἐνεργείας ὑπομεῖναι τὴν βλάβην. 7 Ταύτας σοὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων λόγων, βασιλεῦ θεοφιλέστατε, προσφέρω τὰς ἀπαρχάς· ταύτας ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων πρώτας ἀποφθέγγομαι τὰς φωνάς, σοὶ τῷ γνησιωτάτῳ καὶ πανευσεβεῖ μεθ' ἡμῶν Χριστοῦ προσ κυνητῇ, τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν, τοῦ τὴν οἰκουομικὴν κατὰ τὰς θείας γραφὰς ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις τελέσαντος σωτηρίαν, τοῦ πατήσαντος μὲν ἐνταῦθα τὸν θάνατον, οἰκείοις δὲ τιμίοις αἵμασι τὰς ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτίας ἐξαλείψαντος, ζωὴν δὲ καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ πνευματικὴν ἐπουράνιον χάριν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἅπασιν παρασχόντος. Οὗ τῇ τε δυνάμει καὶ τῇ χάριτί σε φρουρούμενον, λαμπροτέροις τε καὶ μείζοσιν εὐσεβείας ἐμπρέποντα κατορθώμασιν, υἱῶν τε γνησίων βασιλικοῖς ἐναβρυνόμενον βλαστήμασιν, αὐτὸς ὁ παμβασιλεὺς θεός, ὁ πάσης ἀγαθωσύνης πάροχος, πολλαῖς ἐτῶν εἰρηνικαῖς περιόδοις, καύχημα χριστιανῶν καὶ κόσμῳ σύμπαντι φυλάξειε πανέστιον. 8 ἐρρωμένον σε καὶ πάσῃ κεκοσμημένον ἀρετῇ καὶ τὴν συνήθη τῶν τε ἁγίων ἐκκλησιῶν καὶ τῆς ῥωμαίων ἀρχῆς τὴν φιλανθρωπίαν ἐνδεικνύμενον καὶ μείζοσιν εὐσεβείας βραβείοις ἐναβρυνόμενον, πολλαῖς εἰρηνικαῖς ἐτῶν περιόδοις ὁ τῶν ὅλων θεὸς ἡμῖν χαρίσηται πανέστιον, Αὔγουστε βασιλεῦ θεοφιλέστατε.
thought_title: Take up the Gospel and heed its predictions
orientation: Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, is closing his letter to the emperor Constantius by urging him to study the Gospel of Matthew and then offering prayers for the emperor's preservation.
pass_a_gloss: Which divine book of the gospel, having habitually taken it up into your hands, you will find the predictive testimonies laid down about this in writing; of which especially, master, I urge you to pay attention with more frequent study, because of the remaining sequence of the things written therein, of the things announced beforehand by our Savior, requiring much observation with reverence, so that you may suffer no harm from opposing activity. These first fruits of our words, most God-loving emperor, I offer to you; these first voices from Jerusalem I utter, to you the most genuine and all-pious with us worshipper of Christ, the only Son of God and our Savior, who accomplished the saving work according to the divine scriptures in Jerusalem, who trampled death here, and with his own precious blood wiped away the sins of humans, and granted life and incorruption and spiritual heavenly grace to all who believe. Guarded by whose power and grace, and distinguished by more splendid and greater achievements of piety, and exulting in the royal offspring of legitimate sons, may the King of all God himself, the provider of all goodness, preserve you with many peaceful periods of years, a boast of Christians and to the whole world, with your whole household. May the God of all grant you to us, strengthened and adorned with every virtue and displaying the customary benevolence of the holy churches and of the Roman empire, and exulting in greater prizes of piety, with many peaceful periods of years, with your whole household, Augustus, most God-loving emperor.

lemmas.gloss: pertaining to the saving plan, economic

choices.why: Keeps the adjective-noun order and the literal sense of βίβλος as book, matching the source's emphasis on the physical Gospel book taken into the hands.
Literal rendering of προαγγελτικός as predictive, preserving the sense of testimonies that announce beforehand, as the brief's argument emphasizes.
Literal rendering of ἀντικειμένη as opposing and ἐνέργεια as activity, keeping the impersonal force of the source rather than naming a personal adversary.

Renders the adjective-noun pair as a single noun phrase; the glossary sense of σωτηρία as salvation is kept, and οἰκονομικήν is folded into 'saving work' to avoid the awkward 'economic salvation' while preserving the sense of the divine plan.
Uses the glossary English 'King of all' for παμβασιλεύς, keeping the word order of the source where the title precedes θεός.
Renders the adverb/adjective literally as 'with the whole household', preserving the domestic scope of the prayer for the emperor's family, as the brief's argument mentions his family.

pass_b_english: Take up that divine book of the Gospel into your hands as you habitually do, and you will find written there the predictive testimonies laid down about this. I urge you, my lord, to give these your closer and more frequent attention, because of the rest of what is written there in sequence—the things proclaimed beforehand by our Savior—which demand much reverent observation, so that you may suffer no harm from any opposing activity.

These first fruits of my words, most God-loving emperor, I offer to you. These are the first voices I utter from Jerusalem, to you who with us are the truest and most pious worshipper of Christ, the only Son of God and our Savior, who accomplished the saving dispensation in Jerusalem according to the divine Scriptures, who trampled death here, who wiped away human sins with his own precious blood, and who granted life and incorruption and spiritual heavenly grace to all who believe.

May the King of all God himself, the provider of every goodness, guard you by his power and grace, adorned with ever more brilliant and greater achievements of piety, increasing your royal offspring, and preserve your whole household through many peaceful cycles of years, as the boast of Christians and for the whole world.

May the God of all things grant you to us, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, strengthened and adorned with every virtue, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman commonwealth, and glorying in ever greater prizes of piety, through many peaceful cycles of years, with your whole household.
notes: The source text contains 'προσ κυνητῇ' with a space in the middle of προσκυνητῇ, likely a line-break artifact in the manuscript; it is glossed as the single word προσκυνητῇ (worshipper).
The section number 7 appears before Ταύτας and 8 before ἐρρωμένον; these are editorial section markers, not part of the continuous text.

problems.quote: May the God of all things grant you to us with your whole household through many peaceful cycles of years, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, strong and adorned with every virtue, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and taking pride in ever greater prizes of piety.
problems.source_quote: ὁ τῶν ὅλων θεὸς ἡμῖν χαρίσηται πανέστιον ... ἐρρωμένον σε καὶ πάσῃ κεκοσμημένον ἀρετῇ ...
problems.why: English garbles the wish: adds “grant you to us”, misstates who is granted what, and mixes clauses.
problems.fix: May the God of all grant us, through many peaceful years, your strong and virtuous self, showing your customary benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing the prizes of piety.

problems.why: οἰκονομικήν means 'economy/dispensation' not 'work'; 'saving work' loses the technical theological sense of οἰκονομία.

problems.quote: taking pride in the royal offspring of your trueborn sons
problems.source_quote: υἱῶν τε γνησίων βασιλικοῖς ἐναβρυνόμενον βλαστήμασιν
problems.why: Greek says God will increase the royal offspring; English changes agency to the emperor taking pride.
problems.ruling: Greek participle ἐναβρυνόμενον modifies 'you' (emperor), not God; but βλαστήμασιν (offspring/sprouts) is dative of means, not accusative object—emperor prides himself WITH royal offspring, not IN them. English 'taking pride in' misrepresents syntax; Greek means 'exulting in/boasting WITH royal offspring of trueborn sons.'

edits.old: May the God of all things grant you to us with your whole household through many peaceful cycles of years, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, strong and adorned with every virtue, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and taking pride in ever greater prizes of piety.
edits.new: May the God of all things grant us, through many peaceful cycles of years, your strong and virtuous self, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety.

edits.old: who accomplished the saving work in Jerusalem according to the divine Scriptures
edits.new: who accomplished the saving dispensation in Jerusalem according to the divine Scriptures

edits.old: taking pride in the royal offspring of your trueborn sons

fixed: The final wish was garbled: the Greek has ὁ τῶν ὅλων θεὸς ἡμῖν χαρίσηται πανέστιον, with the emperor as the object granted to 'us', not 'you to us'. Fixed.
οἰκονομικὴν σωτηρίαν means 'the saving dispensation/economy', not 'saving work'. Fixed.
The Greek has God as the subject who will increase (ἐναβρυνόμενον) the royal offspring, not the emperor taking pride. Fixed.

problems.quote: May the God of all things grant us, through many peaceful cycles of years, your strong and virtuous self, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety.
problems.source_quote: ὁ τῶν ὅλων θεὸς ἡμῖν χαρίσηται πανέστιον, ἐρρωμένον σε καὶ πάσῃ κεκοσμημένον ἀρετῇ ...
problems.why: Greek says God grants us (the emperor) strength and virtue; English makes God grant us the emperor’s strength, reversing who receives the blessing.
problems.fix: May the God of all grant you strength and virtue, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety.

problems.quote: and preserve you with your whole household
problems.why: πανέστιον modifies the preservation, not 'with your whole household'; 'preserve your whole household' or 'preserve you and your whole house'.
problems.ruling: Greek φυλάξειε πανέστιον means ‘preserve everywhere’, not ‘preserve you with your whole household’.

problems.quote: boast of Christians and of the whole world
problems.why: κόσμῳ is dative, 'for the whole world' or 'in the whole world', not genitive 'of the whole world'.
problems.fix: boast of Christians and for the whole world
problems.ruling: κόσμῳ σύμπαντι is dative ‘to the whole world’, not genitive ‘of the whole world’.

edits.old: May the God of all things grant us, through many peaceful cycles of years, your strong and virtuous self, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety.
edits.new: May the God of all things grant you to us, strengthened and adorned with every virtue, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety, through many peaceful cycles of years, with your whole household.

edits.old: and preserve you with your whole household through many peaceful cycles of years, as the boast of Christians and of the whole world.
edits.new: and preserve your whole household through many peaceful cycles of years, as the boast of Christians and for the whole world.

fixed: Agency: The Greek says God grants us (the emperor) strengthened and adorned with every virtue; the English reversed the blessing. Fixed to 'grant you to us, strengthened and adorned with every virtue'.
Mistranslation: πανέστιον modifies the preservation, not 'with your whole household'. Fixed to 'preserve your whole household'.
Mistranslation: κόσμῳ is dative, 'for the whole world', not genitive 'of the whole world'. Fixed to 'for the whole world'.

problems.why: Greek says “May the God of all grant (to us)…”, not “grant you to us”; agency is reversed.
problems.fix: Change to “May the God of all grant us …”.

edits.old: May the God of all things grant you to us, strengthened and adorned with every virtue, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety, through many peaceful cycles of years, with your whole household.
edits.new: May the God of all things grant us, strengthened and adorned with every virtue, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire, and increasing in ever greater prizes of piety, through many peaceful cycles of years, with your whole household.

fixed: Changed 'grant you to us' to 'grant us' to match the Greek 'ἡμῖν χαρίσηται', where the God of all is the subject granting the emperor to us, not granting us to the emperor.

problems.why: Four variants of imperial virtue-epithet; reader may not recognize these as formulaic equivalents.
problems.fix: Standardize or footnote that these are conventional honorifics.

problems.why: Same addressee rendered with varying titles; reader may wonder if different persons are meant.
problems.fix: Use one consistent title or note that all variants address Constantius.

problems.quote: showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire
problems.why: 'Roman empire' reads oddly; Greek likely means 'commonwealth' or 'realms,' not the modern sense of 'empire.'
problems.fix: Consider 'the Roman commonwealth' or 'your realms' to avoid anachronism.

edits.old: showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman empire
edits.new: showing your accustomed benevolence toward the holy churches and the Roman commonwealth

fixed: The epithets 'most God-loving' and 'most pious' are conventional honorifics for the emperor; the English already renders them consistently enough, and no change is needed.
All variants address Constantius; the English already makes this clear through context, and no change is needed.
The Greek 'τῆς ῥωμαίων ἀρχῆς' means 'the rule/dominion of the Romans,' which is better rendered 'the Roman commonwealth' than 'the Roman empire' to avoid the modern sense of 'empire.'

fixed.quote: May the God of all things grant us, strengthened and adorned with every virtue, Augustus, most God-loving emperor
fixed.fix: May the God of all things grant you to us, Augustus, most God-loving emperor, strengthened and adorned with every virtue
fixed.note: σε is the object God grants to us (ἡμῖν); the English drops 'you' and makes 'us' the ones strengthened.

fixed.quote: increasing in ever greater prizes of piety
fixed.fix: glorying in ever greater prizes of piety
fixed.note: ἐναβρύνομαι means 'glory in' or 'take pride in', not 'increase in'.

dismissed.quote: preserve your whole household through many peaceful cycles of years
dismissed.why: Greek mentions only brighter achievements, increased royal offspring, and God guarding you completely; no reference to the emperor’s whole household.
dismissed.note: πανέστιον means 'with all one's household', so 'whole household' is correct.
